01

The Sysadmin Role

How sysadmin is granted and what it unlocks.
① Role

How it's granted

Not stored in the DB — controlled by the BPM_SYSADMINS env var (comma-separated login IDs), read at startup.
With auth off (dev default), effectively everyone is sysadmin.
With DEV_ENFORCE_PERMISSIONS=true or real auth, only listed IDs are sysadmin.
In ldap auth mode, the Local Accounts Sysadmin toggle can grant it too (effective only there).
The Settings → Directory → Employees table tags them Sysadmin (tooltip managed by environment) — env-listed users can't be turned off from any screen.
① Role

What sysadmin unlocks

Treated as Owner on every map — manage collaborators, approvers, visibility, versions, deletion.
Force checkout — the only role that can take another user's active edit lock.
Every admin-only console under Settings.
Moderation — group approvals, feedback replies/status, the global trash, manual publishing.
Withdraw is the exception — Pending/Approved versions only by the submitter (Rejected also by owner/sysadmin).
02

Admin Console Map

Every console on the Settings rail, at a glance.
② Consoles

The Settings rail

Content — Notices · Manual · Knowledge base · AI chat · AI prompts.
Directory — Employees · Departments · Catalogs · Orphaned refs · Local Accounts (ldap mode only).
Framework — Categories & import (Manage / Status views, linkage admins). Delegated admins see only their subtree.
Database — Tables · Batch jobs (Back up now, backup downloads). Approvals — Approval Queue.
Groups · Analytics (Dashboard) · Trash (Scheduled deletion).
03

Content Management

Notices, the in-app manual, AI knowledge/settings/prompts, and feedback.
③ Content

Notices

Title, importance (Important/General), posting period (open-ended allowed), Markdown body.
Check Notify all users on publish to push to every inbox.
Users see only active notices; the admin list shows all, with CSV export.
Deletion is hard — permanent, no trash (already-sent bell notifications remain).
③ Content

Publishing the manual

/manual holds several documents — each with a format (markdown / sanitized HTML) and a language (KO/EN).
Write inline, upload an .md, or load the bundled copy; preview, then publish for an immediate switch.
List titles come from the first heading — upload KO and EN in the same order so the language toggle opens the matching document.
With no publish history the bundled fallback is served and flagged with a bundled badge.
Click a row to edit, New document to add, the row's trash to delete. The viewer builds its TOC from ##/### headings — images and raw HTML don't render.
③ Content

Knowledge base

A library of org documents the AI consultant cites in interviews — upload SOPs and guides.
Supported: pdf · docx · pptx · xlsx · txt · md, up to 20 MB per file. Upload adds, Refresh reloads the list.
Works only when both AI_ENABLED and the embedding server EMBED_URL (⑨) are set.
③ Content

AI chat settings · AI prompts

The AI access switch at the top pauses every AI feature (chat, interview) without a redeploy — effective availability = AI_ENABLED AND the switch.
Chats are always stored server-side (scoped to user × map, owner-visible) — not a toggle.
Retention caps — 20 chats/map, 200 messages/chat, 180 days (tunable, applies immediately). Loading tips: one per line; clearing restores the 20 defaults.
AI prompts — override the built-ins: saves apply instantly; clearing falls back to the shipped prompt.
While overridden, prompt improvements shipped in code are not picked up — re-check periodically.
③ Content

Feedback administration

Only sysadmin changes status and replies — done locks further replies.
Notifications are deliberate — Send notification (reply, resendable) and Notify status change (once per item).
The "Notification sent 〈time〉" meta row records what went out.
Notes — anyone writes; edits keep history; delete = archive. Permanent purge only via the feedback_notes table view.
04

Directory & Org

HR-webhook sync, the departments basis, heads, and consultant accounts.
④ Directory

Employees & sync

The source is the n8n HR webhook — a full sync refreshes employees plus the departments table (AD only enriches titles).
The Employees tab's Sync all from AD button (label kept) — spinner while running, then a scanned/upserted/deactivated/deleted/skipped summary. One per 5 min.
Auto sync every HR_SYNC_INTERVAL_HOURS (default 24 h, 0 = off), plus per-user daily sync on login.
Safeguards — the sync-preview dry-run API and the deletion cap HR_SYNC_DELETE_CAP_PCT (default 20%).
Departures aren't deleted — marked active=false and excluded from pickers.
④ Directory

Departments & heads

The departments table is the org basis — the single source for the org chart and path resolution.
Heads are determined from EDW position (FRNM) data, tagged Manager on the chain.
Exposed positions — a card on the Employees tab picks which collected EDW titles show in the app (defaults: 그룹장·파트장·팀장·센터장); an app setting, not env.
Stale department and departed-person references are cleaned up on the Orphaned refs tab (two slides on) — it replaces the old Missing departments remap.
Both tables support CSV export (BOM, formula-injection guard).
④ Directory

Catalogs (Roles & Systems)

Autocomplete lists for node Role and System — Role | System tabs, the item list on the left (filter, add), the selected item's alias editor on the right.
Typing an alias saves the canonical spelling (sap → SAP ERP). One alias belongs to one item — a colliding alias is dropped on save with a notice.
Import a two-column value,aliases CSV (aliases split by |, header optional) with an added/duplicate preview; the System tab offers values in use to promote.
Other in the System list is reserved (cannot be deleted, always on top). Everyone reads the lists; editing and saving is sysadmin-only.
The editor, CSV import, AI assistant, consultant interview and interview JSON import all normalize against these lists — unknown systems become Other + source note, unknown roles stay free text.
④ Directory

Orphaned reference audit (Orphaned refs)

Rescan scans 12 places on demand — node departments/assignees, SP designations, owners/collaborators/approvers, owning departments, user groups, category admins.
Results group by value (vanished department path, departed person); expanding lists each reference (map, version, node, role) with a checkbox.
Bulk replace checked lines with a current department or person, or remove them. Node fields are display-only — fix them in the editor draft.
Send owners a Stale refs fix request (one per owner, map list attached); when the owner has left, assign a new one (Owner assigned).
Users see a Stale refs badge, the home Issues filter and warning-colored node icons. Replaces the old Missing departments tab.
④ Directory

Local accounts (ldap mode)

Appears only in ldap auth mode — issue ID/password logins for external consultants.
Sign-in checks local accounts first, then falls back to AD. Throttled to 5 attempts per 5 minutes.
Per account: reset password, deactivate/reactivate, delete (permanent). Deactivate first when an engagement ends.
Sysadmin toggle — local accounts only (directory accounts only via BPM_SYSADMINS), effective in ldap mode; env-granted users can't be turned off here.
Token lifetime and secret rotation (kills all sessions) live in docs/deploy/deploy.md §2.1.
05

Framework Management

Category tree and level delegation, linkage admins, confirmation governance, slot changes, the status board, interview import, filling an L5 with AI.
⑤ Framework

Category management & level delegation

Top toggle: Manage / Status. Tree left, detail panel right — a click selects and expands the row; single-child chains open through to the fork.
Add child · Rename · Managing dept · Linkage admins · Move · Delete are detail-panel buttons; blocked ones stay disabled with a reason. Max 5 levels, maps on L5 only, no duplicate siblings (409).
Renames sync the canvas name; subtrees with linked maps or a canvas can't be deleted (409). An empty managing department inherits from the parent.
Delegation — admins add/rename/reorder under their own category, can't move or delete it (children only), appoint admins one level down.
L5-only admins edit and confirm the canvas only. Top-level categories and interview import stay sysadmin-only.
⑤ Framework

Linkage admins

Select a row, then the detail panel's Linkage admins button appoints users/groups. Adds/removes buffer until you confirm once; Cancel, Esc, or clicking outside discards.
Grants inherit downward — appoint at L1–L4 and every L5 canvas below becomes editable.
Directly appointed admins appear in the detail panel's info line under Admins (three names, then +N), dual-named per the language setting.
Canvases are real maps (mode=framework) but never appear in the map list or SP library.
A major confirm permanently prunes the previous major's intermediate minors (X.0 and the last minor are kept, with a preview dialog).
⑤ Framework

Confirmation governance

Snapshots are a confirmed state apart from publishing — neither they nor the live draft can be deleted; regular map workflows are blocked server-side.
Six confirm gates — all L6 placed · no placeholders · no stale links · all L6 published · no exit-less loops · branches use a decision (all-parallel fan-out exempt).
The Approval tab's Confirm readiness checklist is the single source — one failing gate disables Confirm.
Who confirms — the checkout holder, if they are that L5's direct admin or a sysadmin. Higher-level admins send a confirm request (checkout auto-releases) decided by the direct admin + sysadmin.
Draft visibility — only admins and sysadmins see the live draft; everyone else lands on the latest confirmed snapshot.
⑤ Framework

Slot changes

Which L5 a map belongs to is a slot (assign · unassign · move · hand off · delete) — worked from the Framework pill on the home card.
The decider is that L5's direct admin (sysadmins too). Higher-category admins can edit the canvas but only request a slot change.
A move between two L5s needs both L5s' direct admins (one admin covering both counts once); an L5 without admins falls to sysadmin.
A requester who is already a direct admin applies it via Apply now (toast); otherwise an fw_slot request lands in the L5 admins' Inbox, the map's Approval tab and the Approval Queue (⑦) — withdrawable by the requester, the current owner or a sysadmin.
Sysadmins decide from the queue as the fallback decider — the map's approvers cannot decide slot requests.
⑤ Framework

Status board

The Status view lists every L5 in scope — Path / Latest confirmed / Status (Ready · Blocked · No canvas) with an Open button.
Blocked canvases carry their failing gates as negative pills — Missing L6 · Placeholders · Stale links · Unpublished L6 · Exit-less loop · Direct fan-out.
The home Framework view's category summary card shows the same verdicts under "Subtree confirmation".
Delegated admins see the status of their own subtree only.
⑤ Framework

Interview import — format, dry run, governance

Pick files (multi-select) in the Interview JSON section → file-pill strip → Dry run → report → Apply — sysadmin-only.
Format — interview JSON 0.4 (relations) and 0.5 (externalTasks); 0.3 rejected. Error files skip whole; re-runs are idempotent.
Two-column dry-run report — left: Summary, Needs review, External L6, Category admins, Governance changes; right: file cards → L5 canvas → maps. Many files: scrolling list with per-column scroll and a search/sort toolbar.
Governance changes (re-import) — differing owner, department, approvers or notes become rows with Keep ↩ / Replace ⇄ (notes show a −/+ diff).
Owner assignment — an empty or unknown owner makes the importing sysadmin interim owner (Owner unconfirmed pill) until Transfer ownership.
⑤ Framework

Interview import — landing rules, placeholders, notes

Department path resolution, four passes — exact → leading levels dropped → unique suffix → mirror chain. No match registers the delivered path as-is (remap under Settings → Directory → Departments).
Landing — activities (L7) become nodes, flow edges (seq/branch/loop/bypass) become connectors; branch promotes a decision, a self-loop synthesizes a "Repeat? (auto-generated)" branch.
Conditions, times and systems land as map fields with originals kept as interview source notes. ownerRole lands as the SP designation Role; systems are normalized to the catalog (alias → canonical, unknown → Other + source note, one report row per map). Annual count and FTE land on both the SP reference and the L5 node.
Exact output=input matches auto-link as IO links; nodes auto-lay out horizontally; an editable draft is created right after publish. An activity listing the same item as input and output still lands but gets a warning row (handoffs exempt).
L5 canvas — built or extended from top-level L6 flows. Redelivery only adds nodes and skips a canvas someone else has checked out.
External taskId placeholders — an unknown taskId stays as a placeholder titled with its code; later deliveries or slot assignment resolve it automatically.
Exceptions, VOC, regulatory basis and open items become map notes; L5 entry/flow/open items become category notes. Settle GMP and conditions on the map's Conditions & GMP card (kept across redeliveries).
⑤ Framework

③ Connections · ④ Register

Entering Connections, the AI proposes the L6 flow at once — plan predecessors are the backbone, the entry point is a first-stage card, edges against the plan order become loops.
A full-width L5 linkage canvas with a floating feedback chat (drag, resize, minimize to a sparkle chip). Drag nodes, right-click to add a branch; click a connector to select, double-click for its label, right-click for the menu; auto-save.
A non-branch card has one outgoing connector — a new one marks the old in red dashes and replaces it after confirmation. Chat edits keep the layout; Propose again restarts after confirmation.
Confirm connections → Register: the interview-import screen with an automatic Dry run; Back to connections stays available. After Apply, a completion card (open the L5 canvas · download JSON) — maps publish, the canvas stays draft.
⑤ Framework

② Questionnaire — settling ambiguity

Each card gets an AI questionnaire (decisions · exceptions · branches → activities → basics → I/O) settling who decides, branch conditions, rejection returns, parallel vs sequential, exceptions, start/end — one-line reason per question.
All choice questions are required. Free-text starts blank — [AI suggestion] types the proposal in; blank stays unanswered. Single-choice can take several answers; per-question and submission comments.
No need for detail yet? Create as placeholder skips questionnaire and drawing (Draw again with AI before registration). Failed AI cards: Retry or Skip as placeholder.
Submitting draws that card's flow in the background while the next questionnaire is prepared. Any board row opens its panel (preview · feedback chat) regardless of state.
⑤ Framework

① Plan — cards, stages, external L6

Brief and attachments → Propose L6 cards. Three columns: purpose · attachments | stage rows (top-down order, one row in parallel) | card details (name, summary, role, department, predecessors).
Drag tiles between rows, reorder, or open a new stage (Alt+arrows). Predecessors: right-click a tile and check cards of the previous row — dashed curves, and hovering highlights the linked tiles.
The External L6 tab, or right-click an empty spot → Add external L6, adds another L5's L6 as an external tile (colored per origin L5; no questionnaire, joins the connections only). Right-click a new card → Browse external L6 converts it in place.
Removed cards stay as pending removal (red tile, restorable) and drop out on save or lock. Existing cards keep (dashed, not draggable) or revise. Lock starts questionnaire prep per card.
⑤ Framework

Filling an L5 with AI — entry & sessions

Fill one L5 by talking to the AI, no documents required (sysadmin-only). Entry is selecting a row in the category tree — the detail panel shows tile actions for that level.
L1–L3 — Go down tiles (two columns, In progress n badge). L4 — a name field plus Create L5 and start with AI (duplicate names refused). L5 — Work with AI, or Resume AI session when one is running.
Sessions live in the DB — leaving the screen keeps them; there is no separate list, resume from that L5 row. Pause/resume at the top of the board. Without uploads, Copy external AI prompt round-trips a JSON you import.
Four steps — ① Plan → ② Questionnaire → ③ Connections → ④ Register. Already-registered L6 maps load first as Existing cards (Keep by default, switchable to Revise).
06

Database & Backups

The table viewer, notification purge, batch status, and daily backups.
⑥ Database

The table viewer

A read-only browser with server-side paging, sorting, filtering — it never writes.
CSV export streams all rows with the current sort/filter (BOM, formula guard).
Login records — one row per user per day; the audit view.
Selecting notifications adds a range purge — grouped preview, then a hard delete (no undo).
Notification retention is a fixed most-recent-100-per-person policy.
⑥ Database

Batch job status

The latest attempts of the DB backup and HR sync, per job — last success and last failure each keep their time and summary.
A failure newer than the last success is your signal to act.
Back up now (on demand) — a backup outside the daily schedule. On production (postgres) the sidecar picks it up within seconds and runs pg_dump; local sqlite copies instantly.
Backup file list & download — the card lists ${BACKUP_DIR} and lets you download each file for an off-server copy (sysadmin only).
⑥ Database

Daily automatic backups (prod)

The compose db-backup sidecar — daily after 04:00 KST, plus once on boot if today's dump is missing.
A dump is kept only after pg_restore --list verification; outcomes land on the Batch jobs tab.
Stored at ${BACKUP_DIR} (default ./backups); ${BACKUP_RETENTION_DAYS} (default 14) prunes older dumps.
Server-disk only for now — off-server copies recommended. Recovery runbook: docs/deploy/backup.md.
07

Approvals · Groups · Trash

The global queue, group approvals, restore, and instant purge.
⑦ Moderation

The global approval queue

Pending requests across all maps — group creation, permission downgrades, visibility, checkout transfers, and slot changes (fw_slot) showing map · action · target · progress n/m.
Approve/reject — this queue takes no rejection reason. Map-scoped items are also decidable by that map's approvers; this is the catch-all.
Slot changes are the exception — decided by the related L5's direct admin (or a sysadmin); sysadmins decide here as the fallback.
Renames, SP registrations and Framework confirm requests are handled from the Inbox — approving a confirm request confirms on the spot, so a canvas failing its gates can't be approved.
⑦ Moderation

User group administration

Group creation is request-based — Active after sysadmin approval.
Check the name, members (2+), managers (1+), then decide.
Sysadmin sees all groups, inactive and deleted included.
Deleted groups purge after 7 days in the trash.
⑦ Moderation

Trash & instant purge

Deletions are soft — purged after 7 days; Restore brings everything back intact.
Owners see their own; sysadmin sees everyone's trash.
Instant purge (sysadmin) — remove immediately without the 7-day wait. Trash-state maps only; no undo.
⑦ Moderation

Version workflow — admin powers

Force checkout — take the lock when the holder is away (their unsaved context is lost). Checkouts never expire on their own, so this is how an absent holder's lock is reclaimed.
As effective owner you can submit, publish, and decide checkouts anywhere.
Withdraw is the exception — Pending/Approved only by the submitter.
Approver reassignment — recover approver-less maps via the forced-reassign flow.
Publishing expires the previous version (terminal) — continue via Republish.
08

Dashboard

Live operational metrics and delegated access.
⑧ Analytics

The operations dashboard

Operations — maps, published, in-progress, trash, open comments, your unread notifications, transfer requests.
Version status distribution and adoption by department (denominator picked in the Coverage sidebar).
Login & activity, cumulative growth — 7d/1m/3m/custom period filter (snapshot metrics ignore it).
Recent version events and AI usage (7/30-day calls, top maps).
Access sidebar — delegate viewing to people, departments, groups (sysadmins always can).
09

Configuration Reference

backend .env and compose variables. Changes need a backend restart.
⑨ Reference

Env — auth, permissions, AI

VariableEffect
BPM_SYSADMINSComma-separated sysadmin login IDs
AUTH_MODEkeycloak | ldap | dev — the frontend reads it at boot via GET /api/auth/mode
AUTH_JWT_SECRET / AUTH_JWT_TTL_HOURSldap session signing key (rotate = kill switch) · lifetime (default 8 h)
DEV_ENFORCE_PERMISSIONSEnforce RBAC locally even with auth off
AI_BASE_URL / AI_MODELAI server (OpenAI-compatible) and model id — the in-house GPU uses just glm-5.2
AI_MAX_TOKENS / AI_TIMEOUT_SECONDSResponse token cap (too low = empty replies) · per-call timeout (120–180 s recommended)
⑨ Reference

Env — HR, backups, misc

VariableEffect
N8N_HR_URL / N8N_HR_TOKENHR webhook URL & secret — sync activates only with both
N8N_POSITION_URLEDW head-position webhook — empty disables collection
HR_SYNC_INTERVAL_HOURSAuto-sync interval (default 24, 0 = off) — keep 0 for the first migration
HR_SYNC_DELETE_CAP_PCTSync deletion cap % (default 20, 0 = off)
BACKUP_DIR / BACKUP_RETENTION_DAYSBackup path (default ./backups — point at a NAS for off-server) · retention days (default 14)
MANUAL_URLEditor-toolbar manual button — hidden when empty
Env changes need a backend restart (--reload does not re-read .env). All deployment values live in .env — never hardcoded.

Run it steady

Check the Batch jobs tab each morning, AI prompt overrides after deploys, and department remaps after reorgs.
